implementation_notes: Vapor models the pattern as two middleware stages: an Authenticator verifies credentials from the request and stores the principal in req.auth, while User.guardMiddleware() separately rejects requests that have no authenticated User. Apply both to a protected route group (`app.grouped(User.authenticator()).grouped(User.guardMiddleware())`) so the protected surface is explicit; installing the guard on app.middleware globally would also challenge health and public routes. Route handlers then read the verified principal via req.auth.require(User.self).
pitfalls: User.guardMiddleware() must be added after the authenticator; if it runs first, every request is rejected as unauthenticated (Cannot get User from request).
req.auth is request-scoped storage; caching the authenticated user in a global or long-lived service shares identity across requests.
